c896bcaf	after #295 2026-09-21 — _gen_chain.py --check stops going red by construction - a HEAD-only advance is no longer stal…

Lane P proved at 280e4e82 that the chain was FRESH in the tree that was committed and STALE in the

THE CAUSE IS TWO DIFFERENCES, NOT ONE, AND "IT'S JUST THE SHA" WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WRONG FIX.
Measured by diffing the committed _CHAIN.md against a fresh render: line 41, the build-verdict
line's `HEAD is <sha>` clause, AND line 113, the footer's fixed-point tape figure - 10,480 vs
10,481. The two shas are the SAME BYTE LENGTH and a DIFFERENT TOKEN COUNT. Normalising the sha
clause out of both strings, the shape the brief suggested first, would have left the size figure
mismatched and the check still red. So this RE-ASKS rather than normalises.

THE FIX. check(), and ONLY when the byte comparison has already failed, reads the committed file's
own stamped HEAD out of its build-verdict line (CHAIN_HEAD_RE), and if it differs from the FRESH
RENDER's, regenerates ONCE with that sha pinned and compares against that. Both shas are read off
the two TEXTS, not off git, so the clause stays honest in a tree where git rev-parse is unreadable.

WHAT IS NOT WEAKENED, and it is the constraint the brief set: build() is UNTOUCHED and never sees
the pin, so the chain a cold session reads still carries the honest live comparison - "that run is
at X, HEAD is Y" - against the TRUE HEAD. And --check's own green message NAMES BOTH SHAS and says
"FRESH at the commit it was generated at", never a bare FRESH.

the fix returned 0; run as a script on the SAME TREE it stayed red. Cause measured:
_capture_gate.py:1794 does `import _gen_chain; _gen_chain.build_verdict_line(repo)`, so when this
file runs as __main__ it is TWO module objects and the verdict line is rendered by the OTHER one,
whose global was still None. The pin moved to an environment variable, the one channel both copies
share. That is the #58/#59 class exactly - a check disagreeing with itself across two environments
on one commit - and it was caught because the CLI was re-asked rather than trusted.

AND THE ENVIRONMENT MAY NOT PIN THE VERDICT. A var already set when the process STARTED is
check()'s own scratch channel being driven from outside: it REFUSES (COULD-NOT-ASK), never passes.

J2's own §8 said its rubric was UNFALSIFIED at n=2: "an instrument that has only ever returned

of the mass when it was built to land on level 2. The ladder collapses at the P/M boundary.

of html_to_state — which J2 published as lossy and untested — not a failure of the model.

fee25720	during #267 2026-09-10 — the packaging hole at cause: the lazy `__import__` the AST scan could not see

`local_imports()` (knowledge/_release/_gen_pack_manifest.py:890) read only `ast.Import` and
`ast.ImportFrom` NODES. `knowledge/_validate_receipt.py:635` reaches its mint helper as
`gen = __import__("gen_provenance_receipt")` — a string CALL, deliberately lazy so gate and
generator have no import cycle — and `_validate_screen.py:56,57,99,300` does the same via
`importlib.import_module(...)`. The scan saw nothing, so `helper_closure` in build_manifest()
never claimed the file, and `knowledge/gen_provenance_receipt.py` shipped in NONE of the last
three packs: `unzip -l apollo-spider/dist/Apollo-Spider-v1.0.{7,8,9}.zip | grep -c
gen_provenance_receipt` = 0, 0, 0. Meanwhile the pack's OWN shipped skill
(apollo-spider/skills/generate-from-canon/SKILL.md:291) tells the designer to run
`python3 knowledge/gen_provenance_receipt.py --mint ...`, and both receipt gates name that
command as the remedy. A consumer of the pack could not mint, so could not pass the gate.

THE SEAT IS THE MEASUREMENT, NOT THE TYPED SEED. `HELPER_HOMES` would have taken one name and
gone stale at the next lazily-imported helper [[gate-dont-patch]]; a new `string_call_imports()`
claims whatever the source actually reaches for. Only the `local` side moves: a string call
naming something that is NOT ours stays out of `third_party` on purpose, because
`__import__("hashlib")` (_validate_dataviz.py:277), `__import__('datetime')`
(_validate_type_composites.py:323) and a guarded `importlib.import_module("tiktoken")` are
stdlib and soft probes, and folding them in would invent NEEDS-DEP verdicts out of optional
code paths. The defect is a file that failed to SHIP, not a verdict that was wrong.

886e7e59	after #261 2026-09-09 — #261 N4: the nav label crop was cascade-dead, and the selected row gives back the grey

Dave, verbatim: "the subagents need to be much more careful with the line-height cropping
CSS pattern we have for labels, remove the background grey on the selected state".

THE CROP. The repo's pattern is native leading-trim (canon.css:945-966) plus the truncating-
label exception (`text-box-edge:text text`, so the box does not end on the baseline where
overflow:hidden then eats g/y/p). All three nav snippets had pasted the DEFAULT without
canon's `:where()` wrapper. A bare `:is(button,a,...,input[type=text],...)` takes the
specificity of its heaviest branch and sat at (0,1,1) - above every one-class override in
the same file - so `.nv-label{text-box-edge:text text}` was written and dead, the label
computed `cap alphabetic`, and the descender of "Payments and transfers" was cut.
The list is now wrapped in `:where()` (zero specificity, identical match, exactly as
canon.css wraps it and for the reason canon.css gives), and the trim is restated beside the
edge on `.nv-label` so the pair reads as one decision. Also `.sn-canvas span` -> `>`: the
specimen greeking rule was matching the real `.sn-product` label and forcing it to 12px.

DRIVEN (Chromium, goto file://, ink from the font's own canvas metrics vs the element's
clientHeight): 3 snippets x 4 themes x 2 modes, 336 .nv-label boxes.
  before  272 clipped, worst descender cut 5.50px, 16px label in an 11px box
  after     0 clipped, worst cut 0.00px, 17px box against 15px of ink
_validate_descender_clip.py agrees: Sidebar-nav 4 cascade-dead overrides -> 0.

THE GREY. The current row's fill is removed from the shared item block on all three
surfaces. It was hover's own signal worn permanently, which left hover nothing of its own
to say. Current is aria-current="page" + the 3px indicator bar (a shape) + a weight step on
the label (400 -> 500); the grey means hover and only hover. Driven: the current row
computes rgba(0,0,0,0) with rgb(219,0,17) 3px inset and label weight 500 in all 8
theme x mode combos. The carrier claim is corrected in three metas and two manifests.

Gates: snippets 137/0, coverage 137/137/0, behaviour OK, gen_showroom --check in sync,

0420197a	after #261 2026-09-09 — #261 C5: dvRender.redraw — a re-render that actually re-runs the type partial (#260 A7)

Two reporters (F1 scatter, F1 histogram): dvRender dispatches one `resize`, which re-FITS
and never re-DRAWS, so any decision a partial took from the plot width is frozen at
first-render width. Measured at #260: 11 of 20 bin labels at a 1074px plot are still 11 at
654px, because the thinning ran once.

Two lines of engine: the spec is remembered on the figure (`fig.__dvSpec`), and
`dvRender.redraw(figure)` re-enters the full render with it. Deliberately NOT an automatic
width watcher - ADR-0015 §4 allows exactly ONE rAF-debounced resize listener in this group and
it is dv-behaviour's; a caller that wants width-sensitive marks calls redraw from inside its
own existing handler. An un-rendered figure refuses loud and named, like every other bad call.

MUTATION PROOF (notes/_lanes/261C-probe-a7.py, committed) - the type partial is spied on and
its runs counted:
  first render 1 · after a resize 1 · after redraw 2
  un-rendered figure: 'dv-render: redraw: this figure has not been rendered yet'
The resize count is the defect stated as a number, and the redraw count is the fix.

f84d691f	after #261 2026-09-09 — #261 C3: the zero clamp becomes scopeable — dv-bar-009 is a BAR rule (#260 A2)

Three reporters at #260 (candlestick, boxplot, scatter) and two before them (line,
sparkline) filed the same argument: `if (lo > 0) { lo = 0; }` runs on the line AFTER
fn.domain, so no type can escape it. A candlestick series of 90.41-108.52 held to a zero
floor occupies the top 17% of the plot and every body collapses to a hairline; a
distribution spends a third to nine tenths of its height on empty space.

Their argument is not that the rule is wrong — it is that the rule is a BAR rule. A bar's
LENGTH is its value, so it must start at zero. A price is a POSITION on a scale.
`_validate_dataviz.py` already scopes its own dv-bar-009 check to BAR_FAMILY; only the
engine did not. So this is the core catching up with the gate, not a new policy.

dv-render.js: `if (draw.zeroBaseline !== false && lo > 0) { lo = 0; }`, default TRUE.
NO type in the tree opts out today - which types should is each type partial's own call,
and this lane does not touch another type's partial.

MUTATION PROOF (notes/_lanes/261C-probe-a2.py, committed; same figure, same spec):
  clamped (default)   axis 0-150 (4 ticks)
  zeroBaseline:false  axis 90-110 (5 ticks)
  default again       axis 0-150 (4 ticks)

A. THE CANARY — knowledge/_probe_registry/probe_input_trim_enactment.py, registered as
P-6 in the W-45 probe registry (environment sandbox-render). The class it watches cannot
be caught by reading the repo, because nothing in the repo changes: the day a browser
starts ENACTING text-box-trim inside a form control, every field in the library moves with
no commit and no author. So it asks the browser. It renders a self-contained fixture (a
span control plus input and textarea subjects, same font, line-height:2, zero padding) and
compares each subject's trimmed box against its untrimmed twin; enacted = shrink >= 1.00
CSS px AND >= 5%. Its green is an INVERSION and says so in the docstring: findings=0 means
still inert, which is the state Dave reviewed. Drive at #209: control span 32.00 -> 11.02px
(65.6%), input 32.00 -> 32.00px, textarea 32.00 -> 32.00px, findings=0, rc=0.

SIMULATED ENACTMENT (the watched subjects rendered as a genuinely-trimmed element) makes
the canary sing, rc=1 findings=2; and a browser taken away refuses rc=77 COULD-NOT-ASK both
in-process (empty roots, driver resolution off) and end-to-end (playwright shadowed by an
unimportable stub in a subprocess). A canary that cannot be made to fire is an instrument

WHAT IT DOES
- Seven regions per spec table (a), eight marker blocks: TITLE-GOVERNANCE, PREMISE-TABLE,
  OPEN-ITEMS, DO-NOT-RULE and FENCES-ENVIRONMENT machine-owned; THE-JOB, DO-NOT-RULE-APPEND
  and RETURN-CONTRACT human-owned and carried byte-for-byte, never parsed or validated.
- PREMISE TABLE runs the registry's sandbox probes AT MINT (which probes run is derived from
  the manifest's own environment field, not a list typed into the generator). Every row prints
  command · rc · timestamp · wall · the probe's own last line VERBATIM — no summary word,
  the [[premise-ages-faster-than-rule]] containment. P-3 prints as a DECLARED NOT-RUN row.
- DO-NOT-RULE is generated from store items state=open+owner=dave PLUS rulings with a
  non-empty open field, and prints the measured by-field counter to show WHY the by:Dave
  filter is a constant and is not used (#207 finding (b)). UNCONDITIONED items print as
  declared debt in OPEN-ITEMS, never omitted.
- Ownership is PROVABLE (spec (d)): --regions prints exactly what the writer overwrites and is
  derived from the same REGIONS table the writer uses; each machine region carries a sha256 of
  its own body; a mismatch on re-mint is a human edit and the generator REFUSES, names the
  region and its line span, and names the two legal moves. There is no --force.
- rc vocabulary: 0 minted · 1 measured refusal (hand-edited region / unparseable artefact) ·
  2 bad args · 77 COULD-NOT-ASK (s193-D1) keyed on an unreachable probe registry, never on CI.

7649faa4	after #145 2026-08-10 — post-wrap fix: restore the font fallback stack a1995c0 dropped, and GATE it

a1995c0 regenerated canon.css for the first time since #132 and shipped a typography
regression: --typography-font-family-default emitted as `Univers Next for HSBC` —
every fallback gone AND both quotes gone. Where the webfont fails to load, the whole
system drops to the browser default serif. Found by the #145 wrap sub, which correctly
declared it and refused to patch it; Dave ruled "just fix it".

CAUSE. fmt_value() branched on `ttype == "string"`, but the token's real DTCG $type is
"fontFamily". Once the type was tightened the branch stopped firing SILENTLY: control fell
through to `return str(val)`. Same silent-lookup class as ds-010/013/016/018 — a branch
that stops matching does not fail, it just quietly stops contributing. It sat latent for
13 sessions because nothing regenerated canon.css.

FIX (two changes, not one):
  (a) accept BOTH "string" and "fontFamily", so tightening the type cannot re-break it;
  (b) read the stack from the token's OWN $webStack instead of the module constant, so the
      fallback list has ONE home. $webStack existed for exactly this and was read NOWHERE.
      FONT_STACK survives only as fallback-of-the-fallback. Spacing normalised to ", " so
      the emitted bytes match what shipped pre-#132 — the data moves home, no cosmetic diff.

GUARD (FontStackError, refuse-to-write). The fix alone is not enough: the regression
survived precisely because a non-matching branch is silent, and the output still parsed as
valid CSS. So the condition is asserted on the OUTPUT, in the consumer's grammar, not
trusted in the branch that produces it. Any emitted font-family must be a STACK; var(--…)
alias chains are skipped since the target carries it.

MUTATION-TESTED, both arms, on the real generator:
  1. branch reverted to ("string",) only  -> FontStackError, rc=1, canon.css UNCHANGED
  2. $webStack corrupted to one family    -> FontStackError, rc=1, canon.css UNCHANGED
  control run after restore               -> rc=0, byte-identical to the fixed output
The guard is proven able to fail, not asserted to work.

canon.css line 466 now byte-identical to HEAD~1 (pre-regression); line number moved +2 for
the two rag ink vars s145-D1 minted. Gates re-driven: _validate_dtcg PASS 0/61 ·
_validate_a11y 0 failures · _validate_property_resolves 87 files/0 · _validate_binds_ratchet
PASS. 543 root vars / 189 dark overrides, unchanged by this fix.

NOT RULED, carried to #146: whether the same $type-branch defect exists elsewhere in the
generators — this fix is one site, the CLASS is unswept.

Subject amended #145 (local, unpushed, Dave's word): line 1 carried a DOUBLED
`#145 2026-08-10 — ` prefix. Cause is instance 5 of the msgfile class and a NEW one — the
msgfile was authored with a prefix T3 also prepends, so 'fresh printf per invocation' could
not prevent it. The script's own 'subject asserted identical to msgfile line 1' check is
SELF-CONFIRMING: T3 mutates line 1, then compares the subject to what it just wrote. The
check that works: git log -1 --format='%s' | grep -o '#<n> <date> —' | wc -l  == 1.
Message-only amend: tree, parent (a1995c0) and staged set all unchanged.

b1ca3912	#75-D1: the edge vocabulary closed, and the node registry unfrozen

Dave ruled the six unruled `_decision-graph.json` edge types (UNRULED since #71),
asking for best practice rather than a menu. Recorded in ADR-0012 § Amendment #75.

(a) THE PROMOTION TEST — one of six promoted, five rewritten.
    A new type earns a place only when an existing one cannot say it without losing
    a distinction something else depends on.
      amends/supersedes-mechanism -> supersedes(X, claim=…)   (§5 already makes AMENDED)
      carve-out                   -> bounds(X, scope=…)
      sibling / enables           -> relates(X)
      enacted-by                  -> PROMOTED into EVIDENCE, NOT structural.
    enacted-by is deliberately not folded into verified-by: ADR-0016's register exists
    so "implemented" and "proven" cannot be conflated. Collapsing them makes that
    distinction unsayable in the graph.

(b) THE CLASS FIX — the vocabulary is CLOSED and the gate says so out loud.
    RULED_TYPES = STRUCTURAL | EVIDENCE | WEAK; an unknown type is a loud named
    finding (advisory, ADR-0005 §5). Adding the six to STRUCTURAL was the REJECTED
    fix — it clears six and lets the seventh walk in tomorrow, exactly as these did.
    Two more silent paths closed: malformed-target and self-loop.

    fix would have banked nothing. Edges were parsed live; nodes never were. 14 edge

    T-D15, ADR-0013, ADR-0016) — invisible to the rollup, unkillable, unamendable.

    Registering them would have gone 83 -> 196 and quietly redefined LIVE/DEAD/AMENDED

(d) `Node:` LINES ARE LOAD-BEARING, retroactively. The convention was live in ADR-0015

    LAST `# ADR-NNNN` title in the file — which is how both sub-rulings amended their

4b634eb7	Add _build_survey.py so the failure set is knowable in one pass, and brief #62

Dave, #61: "we are circling the problem and never getting anywhere." He is right, and the
cause is mechanical, not attitudinal.

★ _build_all.py ABORTS ON FIRST FAILURE (:299-301). That is correct for a build - you do
not want step 40 running on step 8's broken output - but it makes the tool's control flow
dictate the METHOD. Discovery becomes serial: fix 8, learn about 10, fix 10, learn about N.
Each round costs a session and NO session ever learns how deep the hole is. #61 burned a
window going 8 -> 10 and still could not tell Dave whether 2 steps were broken or 20.

_build_survey.py asks every gating step INDEPENDENTLY and reports the whole set.
MEASURED: 23 pass · 2 FAIL · 0 could-not-ask · 50 not asked (mutating).
⇒ THE HOLE IS TWO DEEP: [10] _gm_usage.py --selftest and [66] _build_memento_index.py
--check. That is the number no single _build_all.py run can produce.

SAFETY IS THE DESIGN, not a caveat. It runs ONLY --selftest/--check steps by default, so it
cannot regenerate anything; mutating steps are LISTED AND SKIPPED, never silently omitted,
and "not asked" is excluded from the exit code because a skipped step is not a passing one.
--include-mutating refuses on a dirty tree.

⛔ MY SECOND ERROR THIS SESSION, AND THE MORE INSTRUCTIVE ONE. The first cut IMPORTED
_build_all to read STEPS, reasoning that a second parser is a second source of truth - the
same one-slicer argument chain_parts is built on. Sound in the abstract. But _build_all.py
has ZERO __name__ guards, so the import RAN THE BUILD and gutted 33 compliance files - the
second gutting in one session, after I had written the warning about it into two commit
messages myself.
★ The lesson is not "check for a main guard". It is that IMPORT IS NOT A READ, and an
instrument whose act of looking changes what it measures is not an instrument. Now uses ast:
parse, walk, never evaluate. Verified: tree clean after a full survey run.

Also: notes/_briefs/2026-07-31-62-brief.md - #62's brief, written for Fable. Carries the
measured failure set, the diagnosis for [10] (UNMEASURED is an honest refusal the format
never legalised - the fix is neither repairing data nor loosening the parser), the five

claim with its mutation evidence, and Dave's own test: does it unblock Apollo, or is it
Memento improving Memento.

62b6e1e7	The stamp now measures the file it is printed in — and the first draft of the fix cost 107 tape on every future cold read

Dave ruled open 16 (a)+(c) at #47. This commit is (c), plus the mechanism (a) will bind to.
⛔ (a) IS NOT ENACTED: `CHAIN_BUDGET_TK` and the M10 consumer still measure the SLICE. The
cap does not yet bind the file. That is bite 2 and it is deliberately not in here.

WHY (a) COULD NOT BE WRITTEN AS RULED
`build()` calls `read_chain_tk()` to produce the FOOTER, and the footer CONTAINS the figure.
So "measure the file" needs the file, which needs the footer, which needs the number.
Circular. #46 named this without seeing it was a blocker: *"a self-referential delta cannot
be written before the edit that changes it."* That is why the wrapper has gone unmeasured
for three sessions — measuring it was structurally impossible in the old shape, not
overlooked.

WHAT CHANGED — `knowledge/_gen_chain.py` only
- `build()` is a FIXED POINT. Seeded from the slice, which is a strict LOWER BOUND (the
  wrapper only ever adds text, so the first render cannot overshoot). Each pass stamps the
  previous measurement and re-measures the whole rendered file; convergence is the stamped
  figure EQUALLING the measured one, which is the only state in which the footer's sentence
  is true. Converges in 2 passes.
- REFUSES a 2-cycle rather than picking the prettier end. Both ends are false: whichever is
  stamped, the file's real size is the other one. Same posture as every other failure path
  in the module — a stamp picked from one end of an oscillation is the "cheerful zero" class
  wearing a plausible number, which is worse than a blank because it looks measured.
- FOOTER NAMES THE UNIT (ds-021): "the unit is THE WHOLE FILE ... wrapper included".
- Three bites re-pointed and strengthened. ★ The old bite asserted only that *a* measurement
  appeared in the text — which the SLICE figure satisfied happily while the wrapper went
  unmeasured. It passed green throughout the entire defect open 16 records. It now asserts
  the FIXED-POINT INVARIANT: the stamped figure IS the size of the file it is stamped in.
  No hand-maintained stamp can hold that property, which is why #46 broke it twice in one
  session.

MEASURED (cl100k; `tiktoken` installed and VERIFIED before the first measurement)
  file 4,878 tape = slice 4,460 + wrapper 418 · fixed point in 2 passes
  `_gen_chain.py --check` on ROOT: FRESH, exit 0 · `--selftest`: all bites pass

7a988351	dv-004 was enforcing a mechanism its own rule never named — DV-D14/D15 ruled, enacted, render-proven

Dave declined the fix I recommended and asked why I had recommended it. Answering that cost me the
argument and found a defect bigger than the chart.

DV-D14 — separation by GEOMETRY, not a stroke (Dave's ruling, against my recommendation).
I proposed reusing the donut's 2px stroke="var(--page)". He said: "I prefer the geometry the border
will obscure gridlines, may I know why you recommend borders?" One grep settled it: cb5 carries 5
full-width .dv-grid lines behind the columns and the donut carries none. An SVG stroke straddles its
path, so 2px puts 1px OUTSIDE each rect — painting over every gridline down both sides of all four
columns. A surface-coloured stroke only simulates separation when the thing behind it IS the surface.
Enacted variant A (both ends pinned): baseline y=230 and each stack top stay true; the 4px comes out
of segment heights. Accepted cost, stated before it landed: segments understate 2.0–2.6%, worst on
the shortest column.

THE FINDING THAT OUTRANKS THE CHART — the gate had narrowed its own rule.
dv-004's text is mechanism-neutral: "minimum 2px separation between colour blocks". _validate_dataviz
demanded "a surface-coloured stroke >=2px". So a chart satisfying dv-004 by real geometry would have
FAILED, and an agent reading the gate to learn what compliance looks like gets the wrong answer —
which is exactly what happened to me. The gate was not merely failing to catch the error; it was the
source of it. It now accepts either mechanism, with unmeasurable geometry still demanding the stroke
(fails safe). Dave named the structural fix himself and it is FLOATED, not ruled, in _FUTURE-STATE.md
— explore with him, do not build ahead of it.

DV-D15 — data/text/on-series MINTED (Dave's promotion).

coincidence rather than an intent. New role aliases color/grey/white, pinned in BOTH modes, modelled
on rag/text/on-dark; deliberately no alpha channel, since DV-D07 computes contrast from the composite.
type26-013 does not collide — checked, not assumed: its white-only clause is specific to red grounds.

4d0716bd	fix(state-manager): freshness-drift check now reads the bolded Last refreshed stamp

The ADR-0007 staleness gate (_build_live_state.py) existed to catch a drifting "Last refreshed:" stamp, but its regex expected a bare date while every stamp writes it bolded (**2026-07-20**). The ** between colon and digits meant the match failed — "No stamp found" — so the drift-catcher was silently blind for multiple sessions.

- regex: `Last refreshed:[^\d\n]*(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})` — skip non-digit chars on the same line (tolerates **, spaces); [^\d\n] keeps it from grabbing a date on a following line.
- verified: parses bolded + plain stamps; rejects cross-newline; a stale stamp still correctly fires drift (not neutered).
- _LIVE-STATE-CHECK.md regenerated: 1 warning -> 0 warnings, 2 info notes remain (pre-existing).

Build green 37/37.

3af1696c	Gate descender-clip on truncating labels (ds-005); fix current debt

The canon leading-trim (`text-box-edge:cap alphabetic`) optically centres
labels against adjacent icons, but on a label that also truncates
(`overflow:hidden` + `text-overflow:ellipsis`) it clips descenders (g/y/p/q) —
render-confirmed: the Masthead dropdown title showed "Savings" as "Savinqs".

Rather than blanket the CSS (which would undo cap-alphabetic alignment
everywhere) or hand-patch case by case, enforce it with a gate and keep
cap-alphabetic as the default.

- New blocking gate `_validate_descender_clip.py` (build step 27/34): every
  truncating label must carry `text-box-edge:text text` (or `overflow:visible`).
  High-precision — keys off `text-overflow:ellipsis`, so containers and sr-only
  patterns are ignored. Bite-tested; selftest covers same-rule / comma-group /
  overflow-visible overrides.
- Fixed the full current debt, zero waivers: 7 truncating labels across
  Tranche-2/3/4/7/8 + Masthead `.dd-title`/`.navitem-tx`. (List-items + canon
  were already descender-safe.)
- Button audit (the ds-005 follow-on): `.btn`/`.cta`/`.qbtn` are CLEAN — they
  centre labels and never truncate, so no clip. Null result recorded.

ded54985	Assertion veracity gate + handoff; mirror-on-write demoted to PROVISIONAL

THE PERMANENT-FIX ATTEMPT (Dave: "how do we fix this permanently?")
New _validate_assertions.py + _assertions.json, wired into the build (now 30/30).
Environment claims that can rot now carry a machine-checkable predicate, re-evaluated
every build. The load-bearing field is asserted_in: when a predicate flips, the gate
names every document that has just become false — including memory: entries it cannot
read but can still name. Fan-out was the failure mode; the registry makes it visible.
Blockers carry recheck_days, because a blocker stops the work that would disprove it.
Bite-tested by simulating the real failure: dropped a fake Latin .woff2 in, gate went
red and named all four documents; removed it, green again.

Seeded with five assertions, including the two claims that actually rotted: "no Latin
webfont" (still true, 30-day recheck) and "the Latin desktop set IS present" (the claim
that was false for sixteen months, now inverted and gated so it cannot rot back).

AND THE HONEST LIMIT, recorded rather than glossed
Dave: "this is a sticking plaster really, what is causing this?" He is right. The gate
needs someone to remember to register an assertion — the same failure mode one level up.
The root cause is that the architecture is append-only by construction: the capture
ritual has five steps and all five are writes. No read, reconcile, prune or retire step
exists anywhere. _LIVE-STATE has gone 638 to 975 lines in three days and has never
shrunk, so old claims are never re-encountered. Diagnosis written into GOOD-MORNING; the
real fix (consolidation) is queued as a Fable/cold session with a dry-run requirement.

MIRROR-ON-WRITE DEMOTED — I enacted it, then Dave questioned the premise, correctly
Earlier this session I corrected the memory-mirror README (its "the agent cannot copy
memory" claim was false — Glob and the file tools reach it fine; only bash is confined)
and wrote mirror-on-write into the capture ritual as canon. Dave then asked why we mirror
at all. It is not how agent memory normally works, and the evidence is bad: store holds
115 files against 110 live, so it already contains five dead memories and has become the
third source of truth its own README forbids. It exists because we do not trust our own
rule that memory is an accelerator and the repo is the record.
Mirror-on-write is therefore marked PROVISIONAL in both homes, with "should this
directory be deleted rather than maintained?" raised as the open question for the
consolidation session. Leaving it as enacted canon would have had a cold session follow
a rule I no longer believe in.

362be488	Correct my own strike: the Latin WEBFONT blocker was right, and is reinstated

Dave: "we really need the webfonts, this will hinder sharing material."

Earlier today I struck the "Latin Univers webfont missing" blocker as false, having
found the Latin DESKTOP set (TTF + OTF) in knowledge/assets/fonts/_desktop/. That was
wrong. Desktop and webfont are different licence classes: desktop covers design work on
a machine, webfont covers embedding and serving. The blocker never said the desktop
fonts were missing — it said the WEBFONT was, and it was correct. Verified: five script
webfont packs present (Arabic, Japanese, Chinese x2, Armenian), ten woff/woff2 files
each, and ZERO Latin.

Blocker reinstated with the full correction, the superseded text kept in a collapsed
block for the audit trail, and Monotype's actual terms recorded from the Web Font User
Guide now on file: web fonts are licensed for self-hosting, base64 serving IS sanctioned
for licensed webfonts, and fonts must not be distributed via a public Git repository —
with git rm + BFG Repo Cleaner as their prescribed remediation.

What this means for the four already-committed files carrying base64 Univers
(TYPE-SPECIMEN / TYPE-COMPOSITES 2026-07-17, plain + REVIEW, entered at 24accd0):
exposure is real but low — the repo returns 404 unauthenticated, i.e. it is private, and
Monotype's prohibition names public repositories. Any collaborator without their own
licence is still receiving the font, so it is not zero.

What I got right and still stands: the desktop files legitimately supported metric
measurement (the HSBC-vs-stock comparison in T-D3) and local rendering. Those were never
webfont-licensed activities. What I got wrong: converting desktop TTFs to woff2 and
embedding them, treating a desktop licence as if it covered web embedding.

Lesson recorded: a blocker that has stopped work for weeks is exactly the claim you WANT
to be false, so disproving one deserves more scrutiny than confirming it, not less. I
matched a font against the word "font" and declared victory without reading which licence
class the blocker named.

Action for Dave: request the Latin "Univers Next for HSBC" webfont pack (WOFF + WOFF2)
from brand — the same deliverable already held for the five script companions.

58c0561b	feat(colour): promote surface/digital-black + quantify the edge-extremity rule

Dave's specimen-v2 markup turns the drafted rule into a gateable one, and
corrects two claims I made earlier in the session.

THRESHOLDS (from observation, not theory — as dv-019's 135° was)
  saturation ceiling  <= 0.72   Dave picked #B92F1E as the first ladder row that
                                reads clean; 0.78 / 0.84 / 1.00 do not
  minimum weight      10px Medium (EXCLUDED — off-ramp, "don't use this size")
                      12px Medium · 14px Medium · 16px Medium · 20px Light
It is a SIZE x WEIGHT PAIR, not a flat minimum: the required weight FALLS as
size rises, because larger type carries more stroke mass.

TWO CORRECTIONS, both mine
  1. The 700->500 collapse did NOT cause the spidery badge. Minimum is Medium at
     12-16px, so the weight was always sufficient — the GROUND was the fault. At
     sat 1.00 it strained at any weight; at 0.72 Medium holds.
  2. type25-008 ("Emphasis = Univers Bold only") was wrongly invoked to argue for
     700. It governs emphasising keywords in running text, not badge counts, and
     has no bearing here. The 600->500 half of rule 2 still stands on its own
     merits — 600 is not licensed and ships no font file.

PROMOTED — surface/digital-black (#1A1A1A), Dave: "it can be called digital black
or something, that's probably how I'll remember it". Placed in
semantic-colour.json, NOT colour.json: the brand store holds published brand
values and this is Apollo-derived, so putting it there would corrupt the source.
Follows the data/delta precedent. The token carries $substitutesFor, $condition,
$rule and $provenance so the condition travels with the value — the name favours
recall over precision (Dave's call), so the condition must never be stripped
from the token.

THE RULE ASSEMBLED — "reduce the extremity of the edge". Two levers by ground
type, one principle: never add contrast, which makes halation worse. Coloured
ground -> chroma <=0.72. Neutral ground -> digital-black over #000 (17.4:1 vs
21:1). Both -> the size x weight table. Distinct from {#dv-019}, which scores
this 0/3 and is right to; must not be merged.

Gateable now, gated by nothing. Open: Q5 scope, rebinding the 10 literal
#1A1A1A usages, and _PROFORMA-RULES rule 1's stale "open to confirm" line.

c33dc972	Widen 1.4.11 indicator-contrast audit to include border tokens

The verification-edge join was showing Divider's 1.4.11 claim as
not_covered even though it binds proper light/dark border tokens. Root
cause: the audit's classifier matched brand/RAG/interactive/status
tokens only and explicitly excluded anything containing "border" -
structurally incapable of ever picking up a border token, regardless
of validity. WCAG 1.4.11 explicitly covers UI-component boundaries, so
that exclusion was itself a gap.

Widened the classifier to include border tokens. First full-build run
surfaced 19 new gating failures, not just Divider - 4 were */disabled
tokens, which WCAG 1.4.11's own text exempts ("except for inactive
components"); excluded those. The remaining 15 are genuine dark-mode
contrast failures across dividers, tables, tabs, tooltips, form/data-vis
borders, and generic border primitives - left gating on purpose rather
than allowlisted, so the build stays red until each gets a real fix or
a reconsidered applies_to claim.

4 fail (Account card, Cards, Divider, Dropdown - real, previously
invisible gaps), 2 not_covered (Badge, Links - unrelated to borders).

e193ab53	Fix bare :root theme-alias trap in restyled-HSBC build

The hero balance number was rendering invisible. Root cause: the
without-influences-hsbc.html alias block (--ink/--panel/--paper/etc.)
was declared on a bare :root selector, so it froze to html's light-
theme token values instead of recomputing at body[data-theme=dark] --
exactly the gotcha canon.css documents at its own line 495-496. Fixed
by matching canon's own :root, [data-theme="dark"] selector pattern.

Also logged in _LIVE-STATE.md, flagged (not fixed) the Free-buffer
gauge legend reusing the same accent red as live-balance/approve --
one accent doing two semantic jobs, worth Dave's eye.

833bed10	Fix broken Opus expressive-v2 + normalize all spreads to desktop width

Found and fixed a real CSS cascade bug (not a design flaw) causing the
'huge black box' Dave flagged from a screenshot: expressive-v2.html (Opus)
had '.cover__glow{position:absolute}' followed later by an equal-specificity
'.cover > *{position:relative}' which silently won the cascade, dropping
the 520px decorative glow div into normal document flow and pushing all
real content down by that much. Fixed by excluding .cover__glow from the
later selector.

Also found and fixed a comparability bug: 3 of the 10 spread artifacts
(Sonnet expressive-v2, Opus sober v1, Opus balanced v1 -- the last with a
bottom mobile tab bar) were built as fixed mobile-phone-width layouts
(390-560px) while everything else in the set is desktop-width (900-1240px).
Normalized all three to a shared 960px desktop container (removed phone-
frame borders, hid the mobile tab bar at desktop widths) so the comparison
viewer is genuinely like-for-like. Canon's .cn-table container-query
switches to full desktop table mode for free once the container clears its
600px breakpoint -- no content/data/curb changes in any of these fixes.

Also ran and wrote up the pure-inference diagnostic (Dave's idea): two cold
Opus passes on the same data with zero brand governance, with vs without
named influences, to find where the governed expressive-v2's gaps really
are. Finding: colour/type/radius gaps are expected (that's what the
cardinal floor is for); the more useful signal is structural -- ungoverned
runs reached for a genuine organising idea the governed prompt didn't.
Writeup: register-spread-2026-07-05-diagnostic/_FINDINGS.md. Comparison
viewer updated with diagnostic buttons. _LIVE-STATE.md updated.
